newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng Index rises to record intraday high.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index rises to record intraday high.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose in early Tuesday morning trade to a new record high of 12,612, a 53-point gain over Monday's close and 10 points up from the previous all-time high of 12,602.
Turnover had risen to a robust HK$1.8 billion after 40 minutes of trade.
Brokers said investors seemed confident interest rates would remain stable, while the technical picture was also bullish.

"The market is still going up in the short-term," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities. "The market formed a new uptrend last week," he said. "The relative strength indicator is trending up from the 68-point level.
"If the RSI could strengthen to the 80-point level, which would translate into 12,800 on the Hang Seng, he said. "A 200-point advance in the short-term would be nothing for this market."
Brokers also said the market's bullishness derived from investor confidence that there would be no change in the Republican party control of Congress following the U.S. elections on Tuesday.
Properties and the commercial and industrial sector led the market, while finance and utilities lagged in this rally.
Property developers, both blue chips and mid-cap stocks, were the focus of the morning trade.
We saw some good sales and purchase agreement figures (for Hong Kong properties) come out yesterday," said James Robertson, vice president of Salomon Brothers.

The government said the value of property deals signed in October rose 65.8 percent from September 1996 and 193.1 percent from October last year. The number of deals rose 31.7 percent and 121.7 percent, respectively.

Cheung Kong and Sun Hung Kai Properties led the property sector, adding HK$0.75 each to HK$62.75 and HK$87.75. Wharf put on HK$0.50 to HK$33.00, and property sensitive Swire Pacific gained HK$0.25 to HK$67.50.
Among the mid-caps Lai Sun Development advanced HK$0.20 to HK$10.05, while HKR International lost HK$0.10 to HK$9.75.
